details:
1. Project Overview & Problem Statement

Developed by Team ASTROLYTICS, FireSync is a wildfire intelligence platform designed to solve the cross-sensor discrepancy between NASA’s MODIS (1 km resolution) and VIIRS (375 m resolution) active fire datasets. When raw detections from both satellite constellations are combined without calibration, emergency responders face duplicate fire alerts, inflated hotspot counts, and blurred perimeter boundaries. FireSync applies spatio-temporal clustering and resolution prioritization to eliminate redundant detections by ~36%, consolidating raw multi-satellite telemetry into a single, accurate Unified Burning Activity Calendar for global disaster management and forest monitoring teams.

2. Solution Details (How It Works)

FireSync processes raw thermal anomaly detections through a three-stage harmonization pipeline:

- Spatial Grid Alignment: Maps coarse 1 km MODIS pixels against finer 375 m VIIRS sub-pixels using a standardized geographic bounding grid.

- Spatio-Temporal Deduplication: Identifies overlapping detections occurring within a 1 km spatial radius and a 60-minute satellite overpass window. When both sensors detect the same thermal event, FireSync merges the records and prioritizes the higher-precision 375 m VIIRS coordinates and Fire Radiative Power (FRP) metrics.

- Unified Burning Activity Calendar: Outputs clean, deduplicated daily fire logs filtered by global regions (including the Western Ghats, Amazon Basin, California, New South Wales, and Wayanad Forest Belt) so local authorities can track true wildfire progression without sensor noise.

3. Impact & Global Scalability

By eliminating ~36% of duplicate sensor noise from raw multi-satellite feeds, FireSync prevents false alarm fatigue and enables forest departments, environmental researchers, and emergency response units to allocate firefighting resources accurately across both local ecosystems and global wildfire hotspots.

4. Technology Stack Used

- Frontend & Interactive Web Dashboard: HTML5, Tailwind CSS, JavaScript (hosted live via CodePen Projects)

- Data Processing & Prototyping: Python, Pandas, Gradio, Google Colab

- Presentation & Documentation: Digital Slide Deck & Technical Architecture Diagrams

5. NASA & Partner Open Data Sources

- NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System): Near Real-Time (NRT) active fire and thermal anomaly data feeds.

- MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer): Terra & Aqua Active Fire Products (MOD14 / MYD14, 1 km spatial resolution).

- VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite): Suomi NPP & NOAA-20 Active Fire Products (VNP14IMGTDL_NRT, 375 m spatial resolution).

- NASA Worldview & EOSDIS: Global satellite imagery and geospatial visualization reference layers.
